subject: PR creation guidance and procurement readiness - FintechCo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-10T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: PR creation guidance and procurement readiness - FintechCo

Hi Alex —

Great to meet on the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps on procurement so your finance team can raise a PR if that is the path you choose:

1) Commercial path: you mentioned procurement prefers PO for enterprise deals but card for smaller purchases. Please confirm the expected annual commit or single purchase threshold so we can recommend PO vs procurement card. For deals < $50k, procurement card is usually acceptable.

2) Marketplace interest: you asked about AWS Marketplace / Azure Marketplace. We can support marketplace purchases (we are listed on AWS Marketplace). If you prefer marketplace, the purchasing flow is simpler but pricing and contract terms can differ — happy to loop marketplace ops if you want.

3) PR creation + supplier ID: If your procurement system is Coupa or Ariba, the buyer typically needs the vendor/supplier ID to link the PR. To speed things up, we can request to be set up as a supplier under the name "Redwood Inference, Inc.". Typical fields your team will need: legal name, remit-to address, tax id (EIN provided on request), and a supplier contact. If you already have a supplier setup flow, let us know the supplier ID and we can map it on our side.

I attached a short PR template and our PR instructions that finance teams find useful. If helpful, I can open an internal procurement ticket with our Ops team to proactively map supplier IDs for Coupa/Ariba once you share the procurement contact and preferred billing path.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm procurement contact (name/email) and whether you prefer PO or card for initial purchase
- Me: open internal ticket to map supplier IDs in Coupa/Ariba and provide template for PR
- If marketplace preferred: let me know and I will introduce our marketplace ops lead

Attachments: Redwood_PR_Instructions.pdf, PR_template.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Mobile: (415) 555-0199

- We do not currently have a supplier ID for Redwood in Coupa/Ariba. Procurement wanted to know if Redwood can be listed as the supplier (preferred) or whether we should purchase through AWS Marketplace.
- For the first purchase we are expecting a pilot around $18k; so P-Card should be plausible, but I need to confirm with our purchasing team.
- Procurement contact: Priya Shah, priya.shah@fintechco.com (CC'd on procurement distribution: procurement@fintechco.com).

Can you go ahead and open the internal ticket to map supplier IDs so we have that path ready if procurement wants to raise a PO? Also if you can confirm the vendor name and remit details you need, I will pass them to Priya.

Appreciate it — Alex
VP Product, FintechCo

Quick summary of what procurement typically needs to set Redwood up as a supplier:
- Legal name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Remit-to address: 210 Market St, San Francisco, CA 94103
- Tax ID/EIN: (we will provide via secure channel)
- Primary billing contact: billing@redwood.ai (we can copy a person if you prefer)
- W-9 or equivalent for your AP team

If you decide to go via AWS Marketplace we can also provide a marketplace billing contact and link, but mapping the supplier ID in Coupa/Ariba is the fastest route for standard PO flows.

I am attaching the PR template again and a short step-by-step for your AP team. I'll create the internal ticket now and will loop Aditya from procurement ops to ensure quick supplier mapping.

Next steps (I will do these):
- Open internal ticket to map supplier IDs for Coupa and Ariba and attach FintechCo procurement contact

Best,
Marissa
